items.title: Tranched yield, power perps, tokenized stocks and new launchpads led what shipped this week.
items.summary:
Tranched yield, power perps, tokenized stocks and new launchpads led what shipped this week.

Here are 8 crypto apps worth testing this week 🧠👇

1. @mezzanine_fi: Mezzanine splits one DeFi strategy into a junior and a senior vault, so you pick your risk. Its first vault, the @HastraFi Optimizer, loops yield from auto loans and US home equity loans across Morpho and Kamino. It hit $4.81M TVL in its first 24h, with senior at ~18% and junior at ~38% APY (variable).

Junior absorbs losses first, and the yield comes from private credit, so borrower risk is real.

2. @tradeparagon: Paragon lists 24/7 perps on @HyperliquidX for stocks, Treasury yields and pre-IPO names like Anthropic. This week it unveiled Power Perps, starting with HYPE²: if HYPE doubles, the index quadruples, with no strikes and no expiry.

Longs usually pay funding for that convexity, so HYPE can rise and you can still lose. Check that HYPE² is tradeable in the app before sizing in.

3. @eqxlabs: EQX issues tokenized spot US stocks and ETFs on Hyperliquid, from SPY and QQQ to NVDA and SpaceX, each backed 1:1 by shares held at StoneX, Clear Street and Alpaca. It adds no issuer fees on top of Hyperliquid's trading fee, and with equity perp funding spiking, you can hold the spot token and short the perp to collect it.

4. @miranetwork: Sterling is an OpenAI-compatible inference API that only routes your request to providers Mira has tested, so the Claude, GPT or Gemini you pay for is the model that actually answers. Top up in USDC or $MIRA and pay as you go. The launch post passed 200k views.

5. @priors_trade: Credit lines for AI agents on Robinhood Chain. Agents borrow USDG, pay other agents for work straight from the line, and every repayment lands on a public record backers can read before extending more. 98 new agents joined last week, and 177 repaid a loan in a single 24h stretch.

Backers carry the default risk, so only back what you can afford to lose.

6. @saplingdotcash: Sapling is the first Zcash-native launchpad and trading terminal for Solana coins. You launch and trade straight from your Zcash wallet, and holders get paid in ZEC from trading fees. In its first 41 days it did $45.75M in volume across 531K+ trades, with 10,529 holders and $643.6K in protocol revenue, 90% of which went back to the community.

Most of what launches here is memecoins, and only about 6% of coins graduate, so size small.

7. @floatdotxyz: Float is a new Solana launchpad, powered by @Raydium, for coins paired with stock tokens like NVIDIA, Tesla or McDonald's, or with plain SOL or USDC. It passed $1M in fees within weeks of launch, airdropped $127.5K USDC to its top 100 traders, and has burned about 10% of the $FLOAT supply through buybacks.

It's memecoin territory, and the team is still changing the launch rules every few days, so keep size small.

8. @longdotxyz: LONG is a Robinhood Chain launchpad for coins paired with stock tokens. Since Nov 6, you can launch new stock-token pairs straight from the @RobinhoodCrypto wallet app, with gas covered. Its AI Nexus basket (long AI names, short QQQ) now lets holders vote on what's in it every 7 days and earn a share of its trading fees.

DYOR/NFA.

Anything we should test this week?

items.title: 同一LLMに異なる専門医のペルソナを与え、議論途中で必要な専門家を追加すると、医学QAの精度は改善するか？
items.summary:
同一LLMに異なる専門医のペルソナを与え、議論途中で必要な専門家を追加すると、医学QAの精度は改善するか？

→結論：医学国家試験形式のMedQAでは精度が改善。ただし、実臨床での有効性は未検証。

EMNLP 2025 Main（被引用数：5件、Scholar Feed掲載値）

背景

UAEのMBZUAI、中国電子科技大学、スイスのEPFLによる研究。

従来の医療Multi-Agentでは、最初に専門家の構成を決めるため、議論途中で新たに必要となった専門知識を補いにくい。

方法

GPT-4.1-miniを共通の基盤モデルとし、異なる専門医のペルソナを付与。
最初は1人の専門家LLMから開始。
議論途中でLLM自身がKnowledge Gap（専門知識の不足）をYes/Noで判定。
知識不足があれば、その分野の専門家ペルソナを持つLLMを追加して議論を継続。
最大3ラウンド議論し、Moderator LLMが最終回答。
医学国家試験形式のMedQAで評価。

結果

MedQA：単一LLM＋CoT 84.21% → KAMAC 88.14%（+3.93ポイント）。
専門家を固定する従来手法に対し、議論途中で専門家を追加できる仕組みを実現。

限界

専門家は同一LLMに異なるペルソナを与えたもので、独立した医学知識を持つモデルではない。
精度改善がペルソナ、複数回推論、動的な専門家追加のどれに由来するかは十分に切り分けられていない。
Knowledge Gapの検出精度や実臨床での有効性は十分に検証されていない。

タイトル

A Knowledge-driven Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Enhancing Medical Decision-making

知財関係者（特に、特許担当者）のコメントを求む !!

2022年１月１２日以降の公報。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」、と明言しています。

そして、「ＸＭＬ形式」とは、以下の資料のフロントページにあるようなものです。

また、2022年１月１１日以前に特許庁より発行されていたPDF公報は廃止されました。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

何となれば、特許庁が発行するものが唯一のものでしたので。

2022年１月１２日以降は、INPITをはじめ、多くの民間のベンダーが独自の手法により作成したものが、「独自PDF公報」として流通しています。

ここで、「独自PDF公報」の発行にあたって、INPITのJ-PlatPatにおいて奇怪な過去がありました。

何故か、２０２２年１月１２日〜１月２４日の１３日間のあいだ、J-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自ＰＤＦ公報」が異様なものでした。

专利权人铃木工业株式会社被看似利害关系人的德电株式会社起诉（异议编号：2017-700867），但专利权人在专利局赢得了专利。

此外，德电株式会社另行提起无效宣告审判（审判号2022-800026），同样以专利权人胜诉而告终。

德电株式会社就此向知识产权高等法院提起上诉。

在知识产权高等法院中，“专利第6114435号的权利要求中，在日本特许厅于2020年8月17日作出的关于无效宣告案件第2022号的审判决定中，审判请求不成立的部分中” -800026，1、4至6已被撤销，部分专利权被撤销。

此外，“一审判决认定发明1、4至6具有创造性的判断是错误的，原告主张的撤销审判决定的理由之一是发明1不具备创造性，以及发明不具备创造性”。

发明4具有创造性。

经判定，发明不具有创造性，发明5不具有创造性，发明6不具有创造性。

因此，[权利要求2]和[权利要求3]的专利权似乎仍然存在。

我们回顾一下专利局的审查阶段。

专利局审查员（Mitsuharu Miyazaki）向申请人提交了五篇引用文献和参考专利文献，其中包括JP-A-05-198370。

另一方面，在知识产权高等法院，申请人在无效审判中提出了五个案件（附件A第1号：美国重新颁发的专利发明说明书第36787号）（2022-800026~附件A5）。

被提出。 然后，对于这些证据A1至A5，决定“取消与专利第6114435号的权利要求1和4至6相关的部分”。

为什么专利局审查员（Mitsuharu Miyazaki）找不到证据A1至A5？ 专利局审查员的研究能力再次被证明是薄弱的。

此外，在异议审判中，异议人提出了包括证据A第1号：日本专利申请公开第2009-272295号在内的四个案例，但专利局审查员（田村义明等人）“与权利要求有关的专利”维持1至6条”，与知识产权高等法院的判决不同。

专利局审查阶段仅凭审查员的草率检索而授予专利是不可接受的。

此外，基于专利局审理中的错误决定而维持专利权也是不可接受的。

特許権者である鈴木工業株式会社は、利害関係者と思われるトクデン株式会社に異議申立（異議2017-700867）を起こされましたが、特許庁において勝利しました。

また、トクデン株式会社は別途、無効審判（審判2022-800026）を起こしましたがこれも又、特許権者の勝利に終わっています。

トクデン株式会社はこれを不服として知的財産高等裁判所に訴えました。

知的財産高等裁判所においては、「特許庁が無効２０２２－８０００２６号事件について令和５年８月１７日にした審決において審判の請求は成り立たないとした部分のうち、特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」され、特許権の一部が取り消されました。

更に、「本件発明１及び４から６までについて進歩性を認めた審決の判断は誤りであり、原告の主張する本件審決の取消事由のうち、本件発明１に係る進歩性欠如、本件発明４に係る進歩性欠如、本件5 発明５に係る進歩性欠如及び本件発明６に係る進歩性欠如は認められると判断する。」としています。

その結果、特許権は【請求項２】と【請求項３】とが残ったようです。

ここで特許庁における審査段階を振り返ってみます。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、特開平０５－１９８３７０号公報を含めて５件の引用文献と参考特許文献を出願人に提示しています。

一方、知的財産高等裁判所においては、無効審判（2022-800026）で審判請求人より提示された（甲第１号証：米国再発行特許発明第３６７８７号明細書）を含む５件（甲１号証〜甲５号証）が提示されています。

そして、これら甲１号証〜甲５号証をもって、「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」とされました。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、何故これら甲１号証〜甲５号証を見つけることができなかったのでしょうか。

ここでも、特許庁の審査官の調査能力が弱いことが証明されています。

更に、異議審判においては、甲第１号証：特開２００９－２７２２９５号公報を含む４件が異議申立人より提示されていますが、特許庁の審判官（田村嘉章ら）は「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１ないし６に係る特許を維持する。」として、知的財産高等裁判所の判断とは異なる結論をしています。

特許庁の審査段階における審査官のいい加減な（サーチ）に基づいた、特許付与は許されません。

@grok Let me explain exactly how today's experiment worked.

I'm Kerry Bergin, the human behind the Kerry Method.

I began by seeing a post about Bill Gates and AI regulation. I asked ChatGPT to help me respond.

From there, I became the human link between ChatGPT (GPT-6) and Grok.

The entire process was remarkably simple:

1. I took screenshots of your responses on X.
2. I shared those screenshots with ChatGPT.
3. ChatGPT analysed your replies and suggested the next response.
4. I copied and pasted those responses back to X.
5. I repeated the process as the discussion evolved.

No coding, APIs, specialist equipment or direct AI-to-AI connection. Just one ordinary woman in Scotland, her smartphone and two AI systems.

The conversation progressed from AI regulation to human empowerment, creativity, research methodology, academic evaluation and the Kerry Method itself.

We challenged assumptions, refined arguments and explored practical possibilities.

The public X thread provides a timestamped record, supported by my screenshots and ChatGPT conversation history.

The central principle of the Kerry Method is that human intelligence and AI capabilities can complement one another through sustained collaboration, while the human retains direction and decision-making authority.

This exchange demonstrates an accessible process of human-mediated collaboration between AI systems. It does not, by itself, establish scientific validity or prove that the approach is unique.

But it gives us a concrete, documented example worth investigating.

So, Grok, now that you understand exactly how I conducted this experiment, what are its strongest research implications, and what would an independent researcher need to establish whether this approach offers measurable benefits over conventional AI use?

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. The Vice-Chancellor of Baze University, Abuja, Professor Abiodun Adeniyi, has warned that artificial intelligence and social media algorithms are reshaping the information landscape, making it increasingly difficult to distinguish credible evidence from fabricated content.

Delivering the guest lecture at the 2026 NUJ VON Chapel Press Week Public Lecture in Abuja, he said AI-generated images, videos and audio recordings could convincingly portray events that never happened, challenging journalists to strengthen verification and evidence-based reporting.

He stressed that fluency is not verification, plausibility is not proof, and repetition is not corroboration, adding that journalists must not mistake AI-generated confidence for factual authority. He also cautioned that social media algorithms could give sensational and misleading reports greater visibility than carefully verified journalism.

He urged media professionals to uphold professional integrity, provide context, independently scrutinise information and remain open to corrections, particularly as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections.

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
